  • The FT8 Options window no longer overlaps itself at the bottom right (the operator). The Fox/Hound control and the "Skip CQs not for me" checkbox were on the same row and drew on top of each other. Fox/Hound has its own row now.

docs.title: v1.20.4 - 2026-10-22
docs.text:
A patch release. Two of its items are corrections you should know about: the web interface could transmit without the band check that v1.20.3 added.

  • ⛔ The raw CAT command in the web interface could key the radio, with no band check. /api/cmd carries a developer command that passes a CAT string straight to the radio; sending TX; transmitted on whatever frequency the dial was on. The band check added in v1.20.3 never saw it — that check finds transmit paths by reading the firmware's own source, and a command typed into a browser is not in the source. Anyone who could reach your web page could transmit. Every command arriving from outside the firmware now passes one place that reads what it would emit — the dial, plus the tone offset where one is given — and refuses it when the band plan does not allow it. Found here; nobody reported it.
  • ⛔ Radio Menus could start a transmitting test from a browser keystroke. The radio's own Hardware tests menu holds the filter and SWR sweeps, SSB calibration and a diagnostics screen, and those key the transmitter — the diagnostics one at full PA voltage with the SWR protection off, by the radio's own manual. Pressing Enter on such a row, or t on the diagnostics screen, went through unchecked from the browser and from the Tab5. They are refused now, and the refusal says which tool it was. Your radio's own front panel still reaches all of them — that is where they belong, with a dummy load on.
  • An AM listening frequency can be stored in a memory channel (Gyula HA3HZ). v1.20.3 gave the editor its AM button; the frequency itself was still refused if it fell outside an amateur band, which is exactly where AM listening is. A memory is a receive target and receiving is not restricted — your QMX has its own System config → RX outside band for tuning there. So it stores now, and says it is a receive-only channel. Transmitting there is refused by the band check, which is the right place for that decision.
  • Messages that appeared behind the frequency keypad are visible again (Gyula HA3HZ). He reported it as "the response message appears behind the frequency table", and that is precisely what it was: notices were drawn on the screen while the keypad and the band popup are drawn on a layer above it. Every notice raised while one of those was open went unseen, not just the one that made him look — which is why the refusal above never gave him a reason.
  • Receiver audio on the Tab5 wandered in pitch (Samuel W7STF, on WWV's one-second tone). The playback rate is measured from the audio the radio sends, and it was re-measured every second — but the radio delivers in 40 ms bursts, so a one-second count of a perfect stream reads up to 4 % wrong, and the pitch followed that. It is measured over ten seconds now. On the bench the wander dropped from about 0.6 % to 0.03 %, roughly a thirtieth. ⚠ Measured on the bench, not yet confirmed by ear: 10 MHz was dead here, so there was no steady tone to listen to.

docs.title: v1.20.3 - 2026-10-21
docs.text:
A patch release, and one of its items is a correction you may need to act on: WSPR on 60 metres transmitted outside the band.

  • ⛔ WSPR's 60 metre dial transmitted out of band — in every IARU region (Wolfgang DF1KZ). The entry was 5.287200 MHz. WSPR puts its signal 1400–1600 Hz above the dial, so that emitted around 5.2886–5.2888 MHz — about 63 kHz below the bottom of 60 metres everywhere in the world. If you have run WSPR on 60 m on any earlier version, those transmissions were outside the band. The entry is now 5.364700 MHz, and a stored 5.287200 is moved for you when the firmware starts — changing the list alone would have fixed nobody who had already selected 60 m, because the choice is stored rather than read from the list each time. The other ten bands were checked the same way and are inside the allocation everywhere. Wolfgang reported it as a Region 1 problem; checking our own band plan showed it was worse than that.
  • The Tab5 now refuses to key the radio outside your region's band plan. Every path that can put RF out is checked immediately before key-down — the FT8 burst, the WSPR burst, Antenna Tune on both screens, and power calibration — and it checks the frequency actually emitted, not the dial. If it refuses, it says why and nothing is transmitted. It needs to know your IARU region: set it in Settings, or let a GPS supply your grid. With neither it refuses, for the same reason both transmit paths already refuse without a callsign and grid. There is a switch to turn the check off if your licence gives you access the built-in table does not know about — it is a coarse table and has been wrong at a band edge before.
  • ⛔ A QMX+ whose GPS never gets a fix no longer keeps a wrong clock. The radio reports a permanently fitted GPS from its own menu, and that report stopped the Tab5 correcting its clock — deliberately, because an inference of ours once corrupted a good radio's clock. A QMX+ here free-ran 3 hours 17 minutes behind for a whole day under that rule. The Tab5 now asks the radio what time it thinks it is and sets it anyway if the answer is more than a minute out on two readings five minutes apart.
  • If your Tab5 has its own GPS and it is locked, the radio's clock is no longer used. Both receivers were writing the clock and the one with no fix was dragging the one with a fix. The locked receiver wins.
  • The hourly internet time sync no longer throws away the fraction of a second. It set the clock to the whole second below the real time, leaving it up to a second slow until the next sync. With a GPS on the Tab5 this was invisible — the satellite corrected it within the second. Without one there was nothing to correct it, and that error went into FT8 and WSPR slot timing.
  • Skip this exchange, and keep answering (Randy N4OPI). A Skip button ends the exchange in progress and leaves the robot running, instead of standing it down the way Cancel does. The station you skipped is not called again this session.
  • The robot declines a CQ that was aimed at somebody else (Randy N4OPI). CQ DX from a station in your own country, and a US state call when you are not in the USA, are no longer answered automatically.
  • Double-click a different caller to switch to them mid-exchange (Randy N4OPI).
  • "Show only CQ callers" hid the people answering you (Serhiy AA1SL). The filter was meant to hide stations already in a QSO with someone else; it also hid anyone calling you.
  • AM can be stored in a memory channel (Gyula HA3HZ). There was no reason for it missing — the slot could always hold it — the editor simply had no AM button. On a QMX running firmware 1.04 or later.
  • The on-screen keyboard painted the wrong keys gold. _ - . , : and the arrow keys lit up as soon as you typed. Only the shift key is highlighted now, and only while it reads Abc. The memory-channel keyboard also looked different from every other keyboard in the firmware; it does not any more.
  • The spot map's zoom list said "Me centred" and clipped it. It says "Centred".
  • Three settings that were Tab5-only are on the web page: the SelfSpotter switch, and the audio source and line-in gain. The audio pair had always been writable over the interface — the page simply had no value to show, so there was no control to set them with.
  • The diagnostic log was filling the SD card, and the SD card was stalling the browser. Two log lines were being written continuously; the mirror that copies the log to the card then ran every half minute, and those writes held up the spectrum stream — 110 of them cost 40 seconds in one session, the worst single pause 3.3 seconds. The lines are gone and the copy is capped on time.
  • Downloading your configuration now says it contains secrets, at the moment you download it — including your LoTW private key. It said so only in the manual.
  • When resetting the audio does not help, the Tab5 says the radio may not be receiving rather than reporting success. A wedged QMX can stream perfect-looking audio containing nothing; every indicator stays green, and six hours of empty FT8 slots look like a dead band.
  • Every CAT command now leaves the firmware through one place (asked for by Jim, jpwatters). No behaviour changes; it closes a race where a command could be sent to a radio that had just been unplugged, and it is the seam a networked radio would need.
  • Documentation. The manual now says in one place where to find the date (Greg ZL4GW — the main screen deliberately has none), stops confusing the Tab5's own GPS with the radio's, and the memory-channel mode colours it listed were wrong for two of the four.

docs.title: v1.20.2 - 2026-10-20
docs.text:
A patch release. Everything reported in the two days after v1.20.1, one thing v1.20.1 shipped broken, and a correction that matters to anybody who uploads WSPR spots.

  • ⛔ WSPR spots were uploaded to wsprnet on the wrong frequency, if you changed band from the browser (found while fixing John W5JSS's report). The browser's WSPR band change wrote the page's dial figure but never retuned the radio, so the page and the radio disagreed — and every spot decoded after that went to wsprnet under the frequency the page was showing, not the one you were listening on. John's own log caught it: "dial MISMATCH: the radio is tuned to 21.094600 MHz but this page is set to 14.095600 MHz". This is data already in a public database, under your own callsign, with nothing to mark it wrong. If you have changed WSPR band from the browser on v1.20.0 or v1.20.1, treat those spots as suspect. Changing band on the Tab5 itself was never affected. Fixed.
  • WSPR received nothing at all if you came to the page from FT8 (John W5JSS). The receiver needs two large buffers; FT8 had not finished handing its memory back, and the wait gave up 1.8 seconds too early. Every candidate was then rejected and the diagnostic log filled with allocation failures — which reads exactly like a dead band and is not one. The wait now watches for FT8 actually letting go rather than counting seconds, and the same mistake in the other direction is fixed too.
  • The power you set was not the power transmitted, from the browser (John W5JSS). A burst at 2 W with Settings declaring 1 W.
  • ⛔ The AM bandwidth popup had two bad rows — v1.20.1 only. The 10-17 width trim cut the list to four entries and left the count at six, so two rows were built from whatever happened to follow the list in memory, and tapping one applied a nonsense width. The count is now taken from the list itself and the build refuses them if they ever disagree again.
  • AM 8.0 and 9.6 kHz are back (Kevin KQ4DTX, Samuel W7STF). I withdrew them in v1.20.1 because they had never been run end to end. Kevin uses 9.6 kHz daily and Samuel asked for 8.0 kHz back, which is the evidence I said was missing. Measured, those two widths cost nothing over 6.0 kHz.
  • Settings would not save with no QMX attached (Randy N4OPI). The Settings page sends every field on every Save, and one of them — the CW keyer speed — goes straight to the radio rather than being stored here. With no radio to send it to, the whole save was refused with "Save Failed (HTTP 400)", and part of it had already been stored anyway. Now anything the device cannot carry out is reported beside a successful save: "Saved — CW keyer speed was not sent, no CAT link to the radio". A refusal now means nothing at all was stored.
  • ⛔ A Tab5 that cannot save anything now says so (Sergei AA1SL). Sergei's unit received stations perfectly, forgot every setting, and refused to transmit — which is one fault, not three: with no callsign stored, every transmit path refuses. The firmware knew, and said so only on the serial console. It now says it on the screen at start-up, in the browser as a banner, and on the Save button itself. The usual cause is installing with the M5Launcher, whose partition layout has no room for the panadapter's settings; the cure is the project flasher with E at the prompt, which rewrites the partition table. The documentation now warns about this in three places.
  • WiFi ignored the Preferred network on the first boot after an update (Randy N4OPI). "A restart of the Tab5 with nothing else touched restarts, honoring the Preferred Network setting." The preference was being abandoned rather than ignored, on all three paths that set it, and the retry budget was being spent before it got its turn.
  • Web audio went silent after a disconnect (Samuel W7STF). "If the web-UI cannot support audio for hours on end without disconnects, that is unfortunate." It now carries through a reconnect by itself. Measured here: audio returned 16 seconds after the link came back with nobody touching the browser.
  • The spot map now centres on your own station (BD4AHS), rather than merely including it. Fit is still Fit; centring is its own entry.
  • Stations you have worked before can be hidden, not just greyed (Randy N4OPI). This is Randy's original request from the "Exclude stations worked before" confusion in v1.20.1, and it is a separate switch: "Never auto-call worked-before" still decides who the machine calls, and the new "Hide worked-before" decides whether the rows appear at all. Off by default, so nothing changes unless you ask. Per band, on both screens.
  • Re-send stays available until your final is acknowledged (Don WB0LQW). Don's RR73 was missed and the controls vanished the instant it was sent — the one window where the contact could still be saved was the one window with no buttons in it. The row now stays up for the five minutes the machine itself keeps watching, Re-send puts that same final back on the air, and Cancel ends it. On the Tab5 as well as in the browser.
  • Transmitted morse is drawn in its own colour (Samuel W7STF), on both screens. The radio already tells us which characters are ours; it was being discarded.
  • JS8: a station asking for a signal report with the SNR? command is no longer ignored (Gyula HA3HZ). The report exchange was always automated, but the explicit command was read by nothing, so anyone using it got silence. The Tab5 and the browser now say who is asking, and one press of SNR answers them. It does not answer by itself — that would be the radio transmitting with nobody deciding to, and it stays a deliberate press.
  • A BAND column in the browser's WSPR list (Kevin KQ4DTX). The Tab5 had it and the browser did not. It matters most with band hopping on, where every spot sits inside the same 200 Hz window.
  • The browser's Listen button says "Listen" (Bryan N0LUF, Randy N4OPI). Two people never found it, one of them after reading the manual, and Samuel W7STF had to tell them it existed. It was a bare play triangle.
  • RX audio's switch and volume are on the web page, not just in the API.
  • The remote relay can be told to drive only the pin you selected (Randy N4OPI). Until now both GPIO53 and GPIO54 were held as driven outputs whichever one was set to pulse — which is right when both are wired to relays, and wrong if you share the connector with a Unit GPS, because entering relay mode then drives a pin the GPS is transmitting on. Off by default. ⚠ Only turn it on when the unused pin is unconnected or biased by its own circuit: an undriven pin's level is decided by whatever is on it.
  • Documentation. Five diagrams were added to the manual and are on the device as well as the website — the audio chain, the FT8 slot with DT and DTR marked, the WSPR cycle, the clock-source ladder, and what plugs into what. The clock-source list gained the radio's own clock, which it had been missing. The gesture tables now say which one is authoritative. And three pages now say not to install with the M5Launcher.

docs.title: v1.20.1 - 2026-10-18
docs.text:
A patch release. Nine field reports from one week, fixed — and the Tab5 can now be powered off from the drawer and from the browser.

  • ⭐ Power off the Tab5, from either screen (Randy N4OPI). Randy's QMX+ is headless and runs from 18650s inside the radio; when the radio shuts itself off on low volts the Tab5 keeps draining the same pack, and he has already lost a set to undervoltage. There is now a Power off the Tab5 button in the settings drawer, directly under Restart, and the same control in the browser's Miscellaneous section. Both ask twice. It is a real shutdown, not a sleep: the radio is put back into receive first, so a transmission in progress cannot be left keyed, and settings are flushed before the power goes. I measured that it stays off with 5 V still present on the USB-C input, which is Randy's exact setup. The drawer button is in the Advanced section.
  • ⛔ The CAT pause banner was sitting on the QMX's own menu header (Bryan N0LUF). Going to Radio menus and then System Config on a QMX+, Bryan's TCXO frequency changed by itself when he moved off the setting, and twice he had to factory-reset the radio to get serial access back. The pause banner was drawn over the terminal's header. Fixed.
  • The final re-send could only ever send "73", never RR73 (Don WB0LQW). Don's RR73 was missed, his partner properly repeated the signal report, and the machine did not put the RR73 back on the air — it sent a plain 73 instead. The tracker was reading a flag that is always cleared by the time it is read.
  • "Exclude stations worked before" excluded nothing (Randy N4OPI). The box worked; the label was wrong, and wrong in the way that matters — it sat among filters that really do hide rows, so there was only one thing it could be read to mean. It gates who the machine calls automatically, and it is now labelled for that. Whether it should also hide the rows is a separate question and Randy's original request is still open.
  • A station already worked showed as new, once the log passed about 1000 QSOs (Gyula HA3HZ). The worked-call cache held a fixed 1024 entries and its overflow did nothing at all — no log line, nothing on screen. Once it filled at boot, every new contact went to the file and never to the cache, so the decode row stayed green for a station just worked and "Never auto-call worked-before" stopped filtering it. Gyula found it by deleting his log and watching it come right.
  • The browser's Listen button could spend its click before the audio existed (Bryan N0LUF). On Firefox the audio context was created after a round trip to the Tab5, and by then the browser no longer counted it as started by your click. Chrome forgave this and Firefox did not. ⚠ Bryan's silence was not reproduced here, so this is a candidate for his report rather than a proven cause — fixed because it is wrong either way.
  • The web listen diagnostics could not show a stall (Samuel W7STF). Hovering the Listen button reports frame gaps, re-primes and chunks dropped to clock drift. Samuel heard the audio stall and speed up while all three numbers sat still. They now repaint when any of them moves.
  • FT8 on the 3.5 mm jack never decoded anything (Tony, @tony1tf, #19). Audio into the jack, spectrum on the glass, WSPR decoding off that same input — and FT8 silent at every local-oscillator placement. The FT8 slot loop waited for the radio's CAT connection before it would start, and in line-in mode there is no radio to wait for, by design. It waited for something that cannot happen. WSPR has no such gate, which is why WSPR worked.
  • Line-in no longer pretends it has a dial (Tony, @tony1tf, #19). Tony picked 80m and said it should be showing audio frequencies. He was right, and half the screen already agreed with him: the axis was in audio Hz while the top bar read 80m with a band-plan strip of CW and SSB segments under an audio spectrum, with no radio attached. It now says Line-in mode and nothing else.
  • The decoded-CW pane gets a Clear button, and a 2-or-4-line choice (Bryan N0LUF). With enough wrapped text it got hard to find the boundary between fresh and old decode. A click inside the pane still tunes the radio — that is deliberate, the waterfall underneath stays click-to-tune — so Clear is its own button.
  • AM widths above 6.0 kHz are withdrawn (Samuel W7STF, and my own measurements). 8.0, 9.6, 10.0 and 20.0 kHz are gone from both screens; the list now stops at 6.0 kHz. Two different reasons, and they are worth separating. 10.0 and 20.0 kHz needed the decimator run at half rate, and measured on the bench that pins a processor core with no idle left at all and the audio stutters — Samuel had already said the 20 kHz filter should go. 8.0 and 9.6 kHz cost nothing extra: matched 60-second windows measured AM at 4.0 and at 6.0 kHz at the same processor load, so width is free up to that point and those two would have been free as well. They are withdrawn because they were never run end to end — they entered the list on a filter measurement and a listening report, and nothing since has confirmed them. I would rather offer only the widths I have actually measured.
  • RX audio's enable and volume are now on the web API too. Every knob around them was already there — gain, pan, AGC, AM bandwidth, headphone mute — but not the switch that decides whether any of them run. And enabling RX audio needs a restart, which until now was said only in the serial log: the box ticked, stayed ticked, and nothing played. The Tab5 now tells you. The restart itself is unavoidable — the audio codec is opened at boot, before the USB host claims the memory it needs.
  • FT8 pile-up handling (Randy N4OPI). Randy reported the machine working the first caller and the next, then returning to CQ even with a highlighted caller still calling. The slot loop advanced early the moment a decode addressed to us appeared, and the pile-up capture then saw only the decodes published up to that instant rather than the whole slot. That is fixed, and the diagnostic log now says what the pile-up held and why a candidate was passed over, which it never did before — an empty list, a short one and one where everybody was refused all printed nothing. ⚠ Not yet confirmed on air. It needs a live pile-up to exercise and I have not had one since the change.
  • Documentation. The browser's DTR column is now described — it shipped in v1.17.0 with nothing anywhere explaining it, while Randy was asked to report on it. DT is corrected against the band consensus and matches WSJT-X; DTR is the raw offset and is the number that moves when a transmitter's timing moves. The DT column's own entry also now says that it reads -- until two separate stations have been heard. And the audio guide opens with "Getting audio — start here if you hear nothing": mode first, because FT8, FT4, JS8 and WSPR all run in DiGi and DiGi produces no audio by design; then the restart that enabling RX audio needs; then the browser's play button, which two people reported as broken audio when the stream was working and the button had never been pressed; then which of the three volume controls acts where.

⚠ Everything v1.20.0 said still stands. This release adds no new features beyond the power-off button.

docs.title: v1.20.0 - 2026-10-15
docs.text:
You can listen to the radio in your browser, and AM reaches broadcast widths.

  • ⭐⭐ Listen to the receiver in the browser (Samuel W7STF, asked 2026-07-15). Click the ▶ button at the top right of the web page, immediately right of F, and you hear the radio through your computer or your phone. What is streamed is the Tab5's own demodulated audio, tapped after the filter and the AGC, so the browser and the speaker cannot disagree about what the radio is doing. It works even on a Tab5 that booted with its speaker off.

  • The speaker and the browser are exclusive, deliberately. A browser listener mutes the Tab5's speaker and hands the audio back when it stops or the page closes. Audio in two places at once is not something I wanted to build, and one listener at a time is what the design says.

  • Hover the ■ button and it tells you how the stream is doing — frame gaps, re-primes, and chunks dropped to clock drift. On a quiet network all three stay at zero. CW, CW-R, USB, LSB and AM produce audio; in any other mode the button lights and nothing arrives, and the tooltip says so.

  • The card was interrupting the audio, not the network. Browser audio broke up about twice a minute, and the cause was the 30-second write that mirrors the diagnostic log to the SD card: measured at 150–700 ms per tick and once at 4.8 s, long enough to run the player dry. That tick is now held off while anybody is listening, and the backlog waits in RAM, which is what the RAM ring is for. The cost, stated plainly: a crash while you are listening loses the tail of the diagnostic log.

  • ⛔ Superseded in v1.20.1: 10.0 kHz and 20.0 kHz were withdrawn, along with 8.0 and 9.6 kHz. The AM list now stops at 6.0 kHz. The original v1.20.0 text follows. ⭐ AM reaches 10.0 kHz and 20.0 kHz. The AM list already spanned 2.0 to 9.6 kHz; the two widest settings needed the decimator run at half the rate, which costs a whole core, so the rate now follows the width you chose rather than the mode. Below 4.8 kHz of half-bandwidth nothing changed.

  • ⚠ The QMX has no AM bandwidth of its own to match. Its firmware reports a fixed 3200 Hz in every mode but CW, and the eight selectable filter widths are CW-only. The Tab5's own AM filter therefore both exceeds and undercuts anything the radio offers, and the widths above are the only ones that matter.

  • ⛔ Every FT8 action button disabled itself the moment you hovered it (Randy N4OPI and Ryan KK6DZB, same day). A v1.19.0 regression: the rule that locks the dial on the WSPR page had been pasted into the list of hover selectors, so hovering any FT8 button greyed it out. Fixed, and the web checker now refuses that shape.

  • The CW decode strip is four rows, and the row count is one number rather than two that could disagree.

  • JS8 speed is pickable on the JS8 screen itself, not just in the drawer, and a non-Normal submode now says which one it is on the glass. ⛔ A JS8 submode other than Normal decodes nothing and survives a power cycle, so a radio left on Fast or Turbo looks like a dead receiver — the label is there to stop exactly that.

  • The JS8 transmit pane prints the words going out, not "frame 3 of 7", and the frame counter stops counting when the run ends. The JS8 page no longer offers what it cannot do and names what it is.

  • A Flush button in the web UI, and JS8 lines that are addressed to you are marked as such.

  • The SelfSpotter screen says why the feeds are empty when receive audio is holding them off, instead of showing nothing and explaining nothing.

docs.title: v1.19.0 - 2026-10-15
docs.text:
AM is demodulated on the Tab5 itself, and the SWR limit now stops a WSPR burst the way it has always stopped an FT8 one.

  • ⭐⭐ AM, on the Tab5, from the I/Q (Samuel W7STF). Put the radio in AM and you hear it. The demodulator runs on the Tab5 from the raw I/Q the radio already sends, which is why the bandwidth is yours rather than the radio's: the QMX's own AM filter is fixed at 3.2 kHz and sits in its audio, not in the I/Q path. Tap BW in the top bar while in AM and choose 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 or 9.6 kHz. 6.0 is the default. Proven on air on a broadcast station at 7.260 MHz. Until now AM was silent and an AM station meant listening to it in USB.

  • Why 6.0 kHz and not the widest. A shortwave broadcaster transmits about 4.5 kHz of audio, so 9.6 kHz carries the whole thing — but the channels are spaced only 5 kHz apart, and at 9.6 the filter edge sits about 45 Hz from the next station's carrier. On a quiet channel take 9.6 and hear the station in full; on a crowded evening 6.0 is the one that keeps the neighbour out. Your choice is remembered.

  • ⭐ Your SWR limit now protects a WSPR transmission (Bryan N0LUF). Bryan's radio transmitted all night after his Tab5 restarted mid-burst, and looking into it showed that the SWR limit did nothing at all in WSPR — it cut an FT8 or FT4 burst, while WSPR measured the figure, wrote it in the log and carried on. His antenna reaches 5.1:1 in the rain. WSPR now samples through the burst and stops it where it stands, and refuses to arm the next one until you clear the latch. Proven on air: 2.4:1 against a 2.0:1 limit cut a transmission after 11 seconds instead of 110. ⚠ The WSPR chapter has promised this for some time; the firmware did not do it.

  • One limit, one latch, whatever the mode. A bad antenna is a fact about your station and not about the mode you were using, so a trip in WSPR stops FT8 as well and the other way round.

  • The panadapter now asserts receive when it reconnects to the radio. If the Tab5 restarted while the radio was keyed, it reconnected and left it keyed. ⚠ This would not have saved Bryan — his radio's USB had already locked up, so nothing sent could reach it — and nothing on the Tab5 can guarantee the radio stops when the Tab5 is what died. Your radio's own CAT config → Timeout is the protection for that case; it is enabled by default at 120 seconds, and it has to be off if you use VOX.

  • ⛔ The browser acted on the WSPR page's top bar while the Tab5 refused to (John W5JSS). On the Tab5, Band, Mode, BW and Zoom are greyed out on the WSPR page because that page owns the dial. The web page drew them grey and then acted on them anyway. Picking 20 m from the browser wrote the FT8 frequency to the radio while WSPR carried on labelling its spots 160 m — so John saw no spots, a mismatch warning he had to find on the glass, and his own signal reported on a band he was not on. Four of the six things he reported were this one defect. The browser now refuses those four controls there, with a reason, exactly as the Tab5 does. Freq stays live on purpose, so a beacon off the standard dial can still be chased.

  • ⭐ JS8 Slow, Fast and Turbo are selectable, from the JS8 speed row in the drawer and from the JS8 tab in the browser. ⚠ Only Normal is proven on air — the others are built and they transmit, but no contact has been made on any of them. Turbo was thought to be out of reach over the control link; the tone command measures about 250 microseconds, so the Tab5's side of it is fast enough. The radio's side is not measured.

  • A tap on a JS8 station now selects it (Ryan KK6DZB), who held a real JS8 QSO on the Tab5 and sent a full UI draft back. Tapping a row selects that station; the SNR and GRID buttons send to it; free text opens with the pair of callsigns already in place; a CQ is sent once rather than repeating. Three smaller things from the same work: the conversation filter worked on the glass and not in the browser, the target chip truncated a station to "tap a stat...", and the "free text sent" line was overwritten within a second of appearing.

  • A finished FT8 QSO held the radio for a whole extra cycle (Bruce N9JCV). The check that closes a completed exchange ran once per slot, so a QSO that finished early stayed busy until the next slot boundary. It now closes when the final transmission leaves the air — measured at 19 milliseconds on a real contact.

  • The version in the firmware could be a release behind. The version string was baked in when the project was last configured rather than when it was built, so a binary could report a release it was not. If you ever compared the version on your screen against what you flashed and they disagreed, that is why.

  • Every path that can key the radio is now written down and checked — eleven places that can arm a transmission, six of which can do it unattended, verified against the code by a tool that runs every release. This exists because v1.18.0 went out without my knowing my own release answered JS8 callers by itself, and a user had to tell me.

docs.title: v1.18.0 - 2026-10-12
docs.text:
Your radio can now be told a PA voltage it must never exceed, and the Output power control has stopped inventing one.

  • ⭐ "Never exceed PA voltage", a new setting in the Output power section of the drawer. Set it and Calibrate Power's sweep stops there, and the window tells you how many steps it will key before you start. It is off by default, so nothing changes until you set one. This is the only PA-voltage setting that nothing but you writes - Declared power, Output power and WSPR all write the radio's own Max. PA voltage, which is exactly why that one cannot be used as a limit. Use it for a 9 V build, a radio with a known weakness in the finals, or any PA you do not want driven to 12 V. Proven on hardware: a sweep into a dummy load with the limit at 11.5 V ran 43 of the 45 steps and put the radio back where it started.

  • ⛔ Opening the drawer could change your Max. PA voltage, and store the change (Bryan N0LUF). Bryan ran Calibrate Power and found his Max. PA voltage had gone from 11.5 V to 12. The sweep was not at fault - it reads the voltage, restores it and confirms that by read-back. What overwrote it was the Output power control on the next drawer open: calibration deliberately sets no target of its own, so that control found nothing stored, picked a calibrated step anyway, sent it to the radio and then saved it as Bryan's own per-band setting, where it survived a reboot. A control with nothing stored now displays and sends nothing.

  • ⭐ Portable and special-event stations were invisible in JS8, and now they are not. G0ABC/P, W1ABC/4 and special-event calls travel in a frame that needs a different codec, and until now the Tab5 refused that frame rather than risk putting somebody else's callsign on your screen. It reads them now, proven on air: SV2BBO/A was decoded twice on 20 m and appeared in the station list under its full callsign. Three of the 52 JS8 decodes in that three-hour listen were frames of this kind, so it was a steady trickle of stations you could not see rather than a rare corner.

  • Calibrate Power promised 45 steps when it was going to run 43. The dummy-load warning was written once when the window was built and never looked at your limit. The step count is what you use to judge whether you have time for the sweep, so it now follows the limit.

  • The saved diagnostic log was quietly throwing away history. qmx-log-saved.txt is the copy that survives a power-off, and it was set to hold two generations of 256 KB on a partition of 934 KB. SPIFFS cannot reclaim space without a whole free block to work in, so it ran out long before reaching that size and dropped a whole generation each time, a few hundred times over. What you actually got was smaller than the 512 KB it was aiming at, and unpredictable. It now holds 256 KB that it keeps.

  • Your PA-voltage limit now survives a backup. It was missing from the configuration backup, so restoring one silently put you back to no limit - on the one setting that exists to protect the radio.

  • ⭐ The manual had become two manuals, and the printed guide was printing both. The README and the guide pages had drifted into separate accounts of the same features, and the PDF builder pulled from both into the same chapter - about an eighth of the printed guide was a stale copy of itself. Receive-from-the-jack and the web API had no chapter at all. The checker meant to catch this had four blind spots and was reporting clean. All fixed.

⚠ If you have set "Never exceed PA voltage", remember it caps the calibration sweep too. A band calibrated under a limit only describes the radio up to that limit, so raise it and recalibrate if you later want the full curve.

⚠ Everything said about JS8 in v1.17.0 still stands: it is a beta, a full automatic two-way QSO has not been completed, and nothing has yet been decoded through the 3.5 mm jack.

docs.title: v1.17.1 - 2026-10-11
docs.text:
The web page stopped reading the radio's status in v1.17.0. This fixes it, and fills in the documentation JS8 should have had when it shipped.

  • ⛔ The web page showed no band, no mode and no bandwidth, and never followed the Tab5 (Randy N4OPI). The status poll threw an error on every tick, so everything it paints stuck at whatever it had. The spectrum and waterfall kept running because they arrive over a separate connection, which is exactly why it looked alive but stuck.
  • A page that stops reading status now says so, with a banner naming the error.
  • ⭐ JS8 is in the documentation now, with a chapter the manual actually points at, eleven missing glossary terms including DT, a Troubleshooting chapter in the PDF, and receive-from-the-jack, GPS Stats and CW keyer speed written up in the README where the rest of the features are.

docs.title: v1.17.0 - 2026-10-10
docs.text:
JS8 Normal arrives: the Tab5 decodes JS8 off air and can send free text back, with a conversation page of its own. A GPS Stats page with a live sky view. And the 3.5 mm jack can now be the receive source instead of the radio's USB.

  • ⭐⭐ JS8 Normal — receive. JS8 joins FT8 and FT4 in the preset picker, and the Tab5 decodes it on its own: sync, LDPC error correction and the CRC check, all on the device. Proven on air against real stations, including other people's free text arriving intact (F6HCM: SQUARESDR2, 20W, EF ANTENNA 10/(15/)20). Directed messages and heartbeats are read and shown with the sender's callsign and grid.
  • ⭐⭐ JS8 Normal — transmit free text. Type a message, see what it will cost, and send it. There is a Free text button under Call CQ on the Tab5 and a composer under the conversation on the web page. Before anything is keyed both tell you how many frames the message takes and how many seconds it holds the frequency, and show the text exactly as it will go out — upper-cased, spaces collapsed, anything unsendable dropped. A twelve-frame message is three minutes of transmitting and is not something to find out afterwards. A real JS8Call at the other end reassembled a three-frame message of mine and showed it complete, with the end-of-message marker it draws for a finished transmission. A CQ from the Tab5 was decoded by a second station.
  • ⭐ A JS8 page. Stations and Conversation as two tabs: who is on the band, and what has been said. Rows are tappable, and the same page is in the browser.
  • ⭐ GPS Stats. A page of its own under Radio in the drawer, and on the web. It draws a live sky view — the satellites in use, elevation rings and the compass axes — alongside the fix, the satellite count and which receiver is answering. The clock itself now says whether time came from a GPS on the Tab5 or from the radio.
  • ⭐ Your grid, filled in from the fix. If the GPS has a position, the station grid fills itself. It will never undo a correction you typed by hand.
  • ⭐ Both GPS receivers now work, and both are confirmed on hardware. The Unit GPS v1.1 on PORT.A — contributed by Eric (@ericmoritz) — gives you UTC and the full date offline: plug it in and set Port mode (relay / Unit GPS) in the drawer to Unit GPS v1.1. And the Module GPS v2.1 on the 30-pin M-Bus is now actually running rather than supported on paper, which is what v1.16.12 had to say about it. For that one it is DIP switch 6 — the silkscreen group reads backwards until you realise it is named from the host's side, not the module's. Either receiver drives the clock, the date and the sky view below.
  • ⭐ CW keyer speed, from the browser and the Tab5 (Ralph Hellmig). A slider in the drawer above IF calibration, and the same control on the web page. It sets the speed over CAT and reads back what the radio actually took, because the radio is the authority and does not store it.
  • ⭐ The 3.5 mm jack as a receive source — declared beta (Tony, @tony1tf, #17). Tony asked for an audio input for digital modes, and then ran a test build on his own Tab5 to find out where the jack actually lands — the mic ring arrives on the audio chip's third channel, which is the fact the whole feature is built on. An input selector lets you feed the panadapter from the headphone jack instead of the radio's USB audio, with a level meter, a clip indicator and the jack wiring drawn on screen. The signal path is real and measured, built around a 255-tap filter that a test harness caught me getting 33 dB wrong at 300 Hz before any of it ran. ⚠ No signal has been decoded through it yet. The path runs, the samples flow and the levels read correctly with nothing plugged in; that is as far as it is proven. In this mode the USB radio connection is off by design.
  • Tap and hold a frequency preset to highlight it, slide to the one you want, and release to tune. No more mis-taps on a moving train.
  • +6% more decodes, by opening the top end of the waterfall the decoder searches. Signal reports are also recalibrated against the reference decoder jt9, from 154 paired decodes rather than a guess.
  • One transmission is one line in the list again. A single station's call could appear up to 23 times in one slot. The decoder now recognises the same message found at several frequencies as one message.
  • The S-meter read a whole S-unit high below S9, and the browser was right all along. Fixed on the glass.
  • "DT" meant two different things under one heading (Randy N4OPI) — the Tab5 and the browser showed different numbers for it. They now agree, and it stays blank until at least two separate stations have been heard, because one station cannot tell you whether your clock or theirs is off.
  • The battery percentage was wrong in two ways. A charge limit of 80% put "85% (limit)" on the bar, and the percentage truncated so 79.59% read as 79. Both fixed against a measured internal resistance on two packs rather than a guessed one. A failed battery-chip read also counted as a flat pack and restarted charging.
  • A GPS-equipped Tab5 no longer writes its settings once a second. The Unit GPS was committing to flash and setting the clock every single second — 86,400 times a day.
  • More room inside the firmware. 47 KB moved out of the scarce internal memory, and seven task stacks that were sized on measurements taken before their deepest code had ever run — two of them 87% and 91% full — given proper margins. None of this is visible; all of it is the difference between a unit that stays up and one that does not.
  • In the browser, to match the Tab5: the RX audio settings, the dB-range presets, the JS8 conversation pane, and update downloads that continue in the background.

⚠ JS8 is new, and I am calling it a beta. Receiving is proven on air. Sending free text is proven on air. A full automatic two-way JS8 QSO has not been completed yet — that is the next piece of work. Compound callsigns are not handled.

⚠ If you are upgrading from v1.16.11 or older, your waterfall rate will read 10 rows/s once, because v1.16.12 changed how that setting is stored. Set it again and it stays.

⛔ The licence changed from MIT to GPL-3 on 2026-10-09. Nothing about using or flashing this firmware changes. The obligation falls on anyone distributing a modified build, who must publish their source. The reason was JS8: the coding tables it needs exist only inside JS8Call, which is GPL-3, and a permissive licence put them out of reach.

docs.title: v1.16.12 - 2026-10-08
docs.text: GPS time and date from a receiver on PORT.A or from a QMX+'s own GPS, and a check on the date before it is trusted. A GPS receiver on the Tab5 itself, contributed by Eric (@ericmoritz) (#15); a GPS-equipped QMX+ hands over the date over CAT; the Tab5 no longer sets the clock of a radio that has its own GPS (#174); three faults in the date check (royord, #18). SD Files on the web page works again. The waterfall is smoother and its speed is set in rows per second. FT8 decoding about twice as fast on a busy band.

docs.title: v1.16.11 - 2026-10-03
docs.text: The WiFi link no longer dies when the co-processor hands over a full queue (Randy N4OPI, Bryan N0LUF) - a guard of mine refused a genuinely full queue and advanced the counter anyway, so the Tab5 and the co-processor lost track of each other for good. The microSD card is released before any reset, and Eject microSD and Restart the Tab5 are in the settings drawer.

docs.title: v1.16.10 - 2026-10-02
docs.text: Connecting the Tab5 no longer moves your radio to 160 m, and WSPR transmits in the cycle it was scheduled for (John W5JSS). The band scan now saves and restores frequency and mode; WSPR arming moved to its own clock-driven task (5-49 ms into the cycle instead of 1,437). The time sync no longer interrupts a transmission. Show CQs in my run filter (Randy N4OPI); live TX tone panel; RX audio switch says it needs a restart (Samuel W7STF); hosted WiFi relink (Bryan N0LUF).

docs.title: v1.16.9 - 2026-09-30
docs.text:
With WiFi on, SD card writes no longer stop about 30 seconds after boot (Gyula HA3HZ, Randy N4OPI) - a fault that had stood under ⚠ for five releases. RX audio's 24 KB buffer sat in the one kind of memory the SD driver competes for; moved to external memory. Confirmed in the field on three units.

v1.16.8 - 2026-09-29

Static IP finally does what it says, a screenshot that doesn't tear, WSPR that doesn't lie about transmitting, and FT8 that doesn't forget a pileup mid-QSO.

  • ⭐ Static IP and preferred network are now genuinely reliable. Randy N4OPI spent several days field-testing one build after another to get this all the way through - each round found a real bug hiding under the last: the reset buttons erasing the wrong settings partition, a config import leaving the static address bound to nothing, a settings save re-triggering static-IP logic that hadn't changed, and switching networks from the web UI killing the very HTTP connection that asked for the switch. Confirmed on his bench: switching networks or setting a static address no longer needs a reboot, and an address never follows you onto the wrong network.
  • Screenshots download as PNG and no longer tear - /ss.bmp now freezes the region before streaming it instead of capturing a screen still being drawn.
  • WSPR no longer reports "transmitted" on a burst where the radio was never keyed. A flaky CAT link could let the key-down silently fail while the tone sequence played out anyway. Verified before any tones go out; a failure says so on screen instead of logging a phantom burst.
  • FT8's re-send-to-a-partner-who-never-heard-you now tracks up to four partners at once, not one - finishing with station A and immediately working B in a pileup no longer drops A's re-sends.
  • The Audio Settings top-bar shortcut is gone (Gyula HA3HZ) - it was easy to trigger by accident while working the Band/Mode/BW/Frequency pickers. The drawer button is now the only way in.

⚠ SD writes can still stop about 30 seconds after boot with WiFi on. Audio still breaks up with a web page open. The WSPR waterfall shows nothing during the wait between cycles rather than a live band view, unlike WSJT-X (Samuel W7STF) - a real request, not attempted this cycle.

v1.16.7 - 2026-09-26

The idle abort is root-caused and fixed, and the cause was the web interface quietly eating the memory everything else needs.

  • ⭐ The idle abort is solved, not merely reduced. Measuring it settled two things: there is no leak (20.5 hours untouched trends upward), and the internal pool was being emptied 24 times a minute for 60-360 ms at a time, down to 143 bytes - too briefly for the old ten-second instrument to see.
  • ⭐ The cause was the JSON the web interface builds - 495 pieces of a single reply assembled in the scarce internal pool, caught taking 8.7 KB across 311 allocations, while 14 MB of external memory sat unused. It now builds there. 24.1 droughts per minute became none in nine minutes, and free internal memory at rest went from 28 KB to 56 KB.
  • The retry that should have absorbed it was 80 ms - shorter than most of the droughts, and chosen before anyone measured them. Now two seconds.
  • A static IP belongs to a network, not to the unit (Randy N4OPI). Take the Tab5 elsewhere and the old address was still applied: it joined, had no route, and the status just read Off. Now tied to the network it first works on; everywhere else uses DHCP.
  • WSPR names the band it refused, and warns above 1 W before you lose the finals (John W5JSS). A burst is 110.6 s of continuous key-down and a lower PA voltage does not shorten it.
  • Also: refused transmissions appear on screen, the top bar follows a WSPR retune, the date editor steps in months and years (John Dusek), the speaker turns on if the headphone detector cannot be read and the auto-mute can be switched off (Samuel W7STF).

⚠ SD writes can still stop about 30 seconds after boot with WiFi on - a separate shortage, confirmed again and untouched here.

v1.16.6 — 2026-09-25

A hotfix for a crash that is older than the release it was found on.

  • The unit could abort while sitting idle. Found on the bench 400 seconds into an idle panadapter session: a background task asked the C library for a lock, the small internal memory pool had none left, and the firmware stopped. ⭐ Not new in v1.16.5 and not caused by it — that pool has run with a recorded minimum of zero on essentially every build since v1.16.0, and the same abort has happened twice before in other tasks. If you are on v1.16.4 or earlier you have the same exposure.
  • What is fixed: v1.16.5 moved the headphone-jack check onto its own task — a large improvement to audio timing — and that task took 3 KB of the scarce internal pool. Its working memory now lives in the plentiful external memory instead.

⚠ This reduces the exposure, it does not remove it. Everything in v1.16.5 is unchanged and still applies.

v1.16.5 — 2026-09-25

The decoder stops taking two slots to do one slot's work, three things operators asked for while operating, and a crash nobody had hit yet.

  • ⭐ Decoding is two to three times faster, and stops dropping stations. On a crowded band a slot's decode took 11-14 seconds — longer than an FT8 slot, nearly twice an FT4 one — so the answer that decides your next transmission arrived after the moment to send it had passed. Work is split across both processors, and the split was decided before either had run. The second processor also carries USB, WiFi and the display, and measured at 0.1% of its own capacity while drawing the spectrum, so one half finished in 1.4 seconds and waited nine more for the other. Work is now taken as each becomes free, and the slower one left out when it contributes nothing. 11-14 s → 2.7-5.9 s, nothing dropped where 56-68 candidates a slot were abandoned, 3-15 stations decoded per slot instead of 0-3. An FT4 decode now finishes inside its own 7.5 second slot.
  • FT4 stops listening to an empty slot before deciding what to say. FT8 has cut its capture short since v1.14; FT4 never got it. FT4 transmits for 5.0 of its 7.5 seconds, so 2.5 seconds of silence were recorded before the decode could start — landing the result 2.0 seconds into the next slot against a 2.06 second deadline. Every reply was within 60 milliseconds of missing its turn.
  • Pick your next station while the closing 73 is still going out (Randy N4OPI). Clicking a caller in that window answered "Busy: working …" and threw the choice away — and that window is most of a minute, long enough for the station to leave the list. The choice is held and acted on as soon as the machine is free, and the reply is built fresh when it is sent. Same for Auto Pounce on the Tab5.
  • A station calling you out of the blue starts a full automatic QSO (Randy N4OPI). It armed one message and left the rest to be clicked by hand — the sequencer ran only when answering a CQ, which is backwards: someone calling while you are busy is exactly when nobody is at the screen.
  • AGC presets — Fast, Med, Slow and Off (Samuel W7STF), in Audio Settings, with the sliders as Custom. Off is a real bypass, not a very slow setting, and makes AGC Ceiling a plain manual gain. ⚠ The AGC only regulates once a signal is strong enough; on a quiet band every preset correctly sounds the same.
  • The WiFi page says which network you are actually on, and warns when a preferred network will take over at the next restart (Randy N4OPI).
  • Switching between FT8 and FT4 could crash the unit. Buffers were freed after a four second wait whether or not the decoder had finished — and on a busy band it had not. Non-deterministic, which is why it survived.
  • One bad reading no longer switches the speaker, and following the jack moved off the audio path — late writes to the sound hardware fell from about 7% to under 2%. Audio is measurably cleaner than v1.16.4 even with the jack untouched.

⚠ Still unfixed: audio breaks up while a web page is open; with WiFi on, SD writes stop within about 30 seconds of boot.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.16.4 — 2026-09-25

Four faults operators found in their own shacks, headphones behaving as everyone expected, and the measurement that finally explains the SD card.

  • A station answering your CQ is answered in the very next slot — every time, not half the time. Decoding is shared between the Tab5's two processors, and only one of them was allowed to act the moment it spotted somebody calling you. Which one found your caller was chance, so the identical situation replied immediately about half the time and a full 30-second cycle late the rest. "Sometimes it works well, other times the transmission is delayed" was exactly right, and that variability was the fault (Gyula HA3HZ). Tested on the air over three contacts.
  • Waiting for a busy station really is capped at six minutes now. When the station you called is working somebody else the Tab5 stands by rather than transmit over them — and the six-minute limit it claimed never worked: the counter reset instead of stopping, so it could wait over half an hour. Each held slot also cancelled the call it had just queued, so it never got back to calling them either. One fault, both symptoms — including "it continues to wait rather than calling again after an RR73".
  • Headphones silence the internal speaker (Roy KI0ER). Sound used to come out of both at once, which made headphones close to useless in a quiet shack. Plug in, the speaker stops; unplug, it comes back. Nothing to set.
  • Resource Management is now Audio Settings, and has its own button in the settings drawer, just below SelfSpotter. It is volume, AGC, binaural and the panoramic split — the old name described the machinery rather than the purpose. The top-bar long-press still works, but it shared its area with the Band, Mode, BW and Frequency pickers, so it was easy to open the wrong thing.
  • Preferred network actually decides which WiFi you join (Randy N4OPI). Added in v1.16.3, it was only consulted after the Tab5 had failed to connect twice — so it worked when your usual network was down and did nothing in the case it was written for. It also needed a reboot. Both fixed. A Network name typed with the password left blank is no longer silently discarded either, and both fields now list the networks your Tab5 actually remembers.
  • A restart caused by a power brownout now says so (Samuel W7STF). His unit rebooted repeatedly while he listened, and he reasonably suspected his own hardware — his logs held ten brownout resets, which is the supply rail dipping, not a crash and not a fault in the Tab5. The firmware knew every time and told nobody. Now it is on screen at start-up.
  • The FT8 transmit tone saves from the settings page. It said Saved, wrote the value down, and never told the radio.

⭐ The SD card was never the problem. The recurring "SD dot goes yellow and writes stop" is root-caused: the card driver is refused a memory buffer, so the write never reaches a card that is mounted and perfectly healthy. This is why reformatting, reseating and replacing cards has never helped anybody. Every diagnostic log now opens with a start-up memory ledger showing where that memory went — the audio output stage alone accounts for 46.5 KB of it. The same shortage is what silently stops Bluetooth starting when the symbol reads grey with the box still ticked. Diagnosed and documented; not yet reduced, because the remedy trades against audio quality and deserves proper testing first.

Audio and binaural CW remain a beta, and audio still breaks up while a web page is open — close it while you listen.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.16.3 — 2026-09-23

The audio fix v1.16.2 was meant to be, all four audio controls on one page, and three things that were quietly misreporting their own state.

  • The crackle really is gone this time. v1.16.2 said the break-ups were fixed, and they were — but what shipped was the first of five attempts at the correction, and you could still hear it working. The real fault was a buffer with room for one extra sample where the corrector needed dozens, and a counter that ran backwards when it hit that wall and started inventing waveform. That is why it crackled even on an empty band with no signal at all.
  • Every audio control is now in one window. RX Volume has moved out of the settings drawer and into Resource Management, next to the gain controls that decide the same thing your ears hear. ⚠ The drawer's RX Audio section is gone completely, including its on/off tick box — long-press the top bar to reach it now.
  • "Gain" is now called AGC Ceiling, and goes up to 1500. It was never a plain gain: it sets how hard the automatic gain is allowed to lift a weak signal. The old name had people hunting for an AGC that was already there. The extra range is for the Tab5's own speaker, which needs more than the old ceiling of 800 allowed.
  • Attack and Release are yours to set now — 1–50 ms and 10–500 ms. Shorter attack catches sharp CW edges; longer release is steadier on CW, shorter follows speech better. Both are remembered and travel in a config backup.
  • A GPS that takes a while to lock is no longer missed (John W5JSS). Detection ran once, about 45 seconds after switching on, and whatever it decided then stuck for the rest of the session — so a receiver still hunting for satellites was written off as "no GPS" until you rebooted. A QMX+ here locked 25 minutes after boot and is now picked up automatically. If yours still says NTP, check the radio's own GPS viewer: the panadapter only accepts a fix that genuinely agrees with network time.
  • WSPR hands the radio back. WSPR has to transmit in Digi, and it was leaving the radio there afterwards — every cycle, for ever. Since the QMX remembers its mode, it then powered up in Digi too, which looked like the mode failing to save. It now puts back whatever mode it interrupted. ⚠ Built and reasoned through, but not yet watched through a live WSPR cycle.
  • Preferred network (Randy N4OPI). The Tab5 remembers up to six networks, but when it fell back it always took the loudest — wrong if you have a DMZ next to a house network. Name the one you want in the web page's WiFi settings and it wins whenever it is in range. Leave it blank and nothing changes.
  • The SD dot tells the truth. It turned yellow about ten seconds into any WiFi session and stayed yellow regardless — the same colour on a perfectly healthy card and on one where every single write was failing. Green now means a write actually reached the card in the last 90 seconds.

Audio and binaural CW remain a beta, and audio still breaks up while a web page is open — close it while you listen. That one was measured again this cycle and the most likely cause was tested and ruled out, so it is still open.

⚠ With WiFi on, writes to the microSD card stop about 30 seconds after start-up on at least one bench unit — the memory the card driver needs is taken by WiFi and never comes back. Your start-up backup always lands; nothing after it does. Known, measured, not yet fixed.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.16.2 — 2026-09-22

Audio you can listen to for an hour, and a microSD card that stops being thrown away.

  • A strong signal can no longer take your ears off. The automatic gain lifted everything to within a hair of full scale, so a loud station arrived at maximum and anything faster than the gain could follow ran into a hard clip — loud and harsh at once. A proper peak limiter now holds the peaks and leaves the average level alone, so quiet stations are as loud as they were.
  • The break-ups in the audio are gone, and they were never the CPU. Your QMX sends about 47,885 samples a second; the Tab5's codec plays exactly 48,000, from its own crystal. Nothing reconciled the two, so the buffer emptied a little every second and a fragment of silence was played instead — roughly every three seconds, with no error recorded anywhere. The output is now locked to the clock.
  • LSB is fixed (Gyula HA3HZ). The audio was taken from the wrong side of the dial, so you heard whatever was mirrored there instead of the station on screen. The spectrum had always been right; only the audio was wrong.
  • If your audio is too quiet, check which control you are on (Samuel W7STF). The sliders marked Volume stop at 100. Gain — the one that lifts weak signals — is on the RX Audio line in Resource Management and runs 50 to 800.
  • A working microSD card is no longer discarded (Dennis WN4FLA). The card mounted, the first diagnostic-log write failed, and after five tries the Tab5 decided the card had been pulled — green dot, then yellow, then grey, for the rest of the session. The card was never gone; every other file on it wrote perfectly at the same moment. The log also never rotated at its 5 MB limit on any unit with WiFi on, and the Tab5 now tells you how full the card is when a write fails.
  • Pause is on the web page (Randy N4OPI), with play/pause symbols, and pressing it again takes the pause back. Pausing no longer costs you the contact (Gyula HA3HZ) — the quiet slot it creates was being counted against the six cycles before giving up.
  • Reboot the Tab5 from the browser (Randy N4OPI) — Miscellaneous menu.
  • KM and AGE no longer collide on the decode list (Gyula HA3HZ).

Audio and binaural CW remain a beta. Audio still stutters while a browser has the panadapter open — that is the Tab5's first processor running out of room, it is measured, and it is next. Close the web page while you listen.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.16.1 — 2026-09-22

The fixes you asked for after v1.16.0 — and one thing v1.16.0's notes promised but never actually shipped.

  • The Pause button is there now. It was written up in the v1.16.0 notes and then drawn just off the edge of its panel, so nobody could find it — Randy N4OPI reported it missing and he was right. It is the fourth button in the mid-QSO row, it works while calling CQ as well as mid-exchange, and it reads Paused while armed so you can see it is doing something. Skipping a slot on purpose also no longer counts against giving up on the contact.
  • A Gain control for the audio. Several of you said the audio was very quiet even at full volume (Samuel W7STF, Bruce N9JCV) — that was the automatic gain's ceiling, not your volume control, and there was no way to reach it. It is now a slider on the RX Audio line in Resource Management.
  • The three panoramic CW controls are real controls. Pan Width, Blend and Overlap were described as adjustable while you listen, and had no control anywhere on the device. They sit under Binaural CW now. All four settings are remembered across a restart and are carried in a config backup.
  • SSB is intelligible again. (Gyula HA3HZ) The automatic gain was reacting about eight times too slowly for speech, clipping the start of every syllable and then staying ducked through the ones after. Morse never showed it, because a steady tone never tests how fast the control moves.
  • WSPR keeps to its minutes. (John W5JSS) A 20-minute schedule could walk off the minutes it started on after a few hours. The schedule is now anchored to the clock, so "2 transmits in every 20 minutes" means the same minutes every time, and a missed cycle or a restart no longer shifts it.
  • Resource Management is easier to read — Binaural CW sits with RX Audio, the network feeds are grouped together, and controls that cannot do anything yet are greyed out properly instead of looking live.

!!! warning "Switch the QMX on after the Tab5 has settled"

Wait until the spectrum is running and WiFi shows a network, then power the radio.
Switching it on while the Tab5 is still starting up leaves the Tab5 short of memory
for the rest of the session — most visibly, the web interface may stop responding.
This is a firmware limitation and it is being worked on.

Audio remains a beta. It is there to be tried and reported on. Binaural CW works best at 300 Hz bandwidth and up; below 200 Hz there is little separation to be had.

v1.16.0 — 2026-09-21

Audio on the Tab5, as a beta — and a Pause button during a QSO.

  • You can listen to the radio through the Tab5. The I/Q the QMX already sends is turned into sound on the device. This is new ground, and the whole audio part is a beta: it is there to be tried and reported on, not to be relied on yet.
  • Panoramic CW split. Two stations on different frequencies are placed left and right across the stereo image instead of landing on top of each other. Three controls are live while you listen — pan width (how far apart they sit), pan blend (how much of the effect is mixed in) and overlap (how wide a slice each side takes). You adjust them by ear, mid-QSO, not in a menu.
  • Binaural CW is a first implementation. Use it at 300 Hz bandwidth and up. Below 200 Hz do not expect much separation — at that point the two signals share too much of the audio passband for any amount of panning to pull them apart. That is a limit of the bandwidth, not of the setting.
  • Audio costs resources, so not everything can be on at once. Long-press the top bar on the Panadapter page to open Resource Management — that is where audio is switched on and off, and where you can see what it is competing with. Expect to turn something else down to make room.
  • What is planned next: the same audio features in the web interface, with only the I/Q channels sent to the PC and the processing done there — so your computer does the work instead of the Tab5. Full detail, limits and the reasoning are in the Audio guide.
  • I am looking forward to the feedback. What works, what does not, which bandwidth you actually use, and where you hit the resource limits.
  • A Pause button during a QSO (Randy N4OPI). Skip a single transmission to check whether your slot is still clear, then carry on with the same message. Cancel breaks the exchange; Pause does not. It sits alongside Re-send / RR73 / 73 and appears only while an exchange is running.

v1.15.1 — 2026-09-19

More working memory for WSPR, one file for the diagnostic download, and the same column order on every list.

  • WSPR has more room to work in. The routine that picks out signals needs a large block of memory, and on a busy page it could be left with only just enough. When it came up short it simply reported nothing found for that cycle — so a cycle could come back empty with traces plainly visible on the waterfall, most often after moving between pages. Freeing 2.8 MB removes the squeeze, and if it is ever short again it now says so instead of going quiet.
  • The diagnostic download is a single zip file. Both logs now arrive as one qmx-diag-….zip you can attach to an email, instead of two separate downloads your browser had to be persuaded to accept. Behind that single file the browser still fetches the two logs from the Tab5, and it now does so one at a time: downloading the live log clears it from the Tab5, so a transfer that failed used to take the log with it. (John W5JSS.)
  • One column order on every list. FT8, the SelfSpotter list and WSPR now read left to right the same way, with capitalised headings, so your eye lands in the same place on each screen. The SelfSpotter list gains a GRID column — the locator the receiving station actually sent.
  • Calibrate Power warns if your radio is turned down. It never sweeps past the Max PA voltage your radio is holding, which is right — but if a WSPR session left that at 6 V, the calibration measured only as far as 6 V and then held you there. It now says "Radio max is only 6.0V — raise it first!" in amber before you start. (Rick W5NR.)
  • WSPR will not beacon on a band you have not calibrated. The power figure travels inside the transmitted message and is published worldwide, so a burst on an uncalibrated band would tell everyone a number the Tab5 cannot stand behind. Switching transmit on now says which band needs calibrating instead of starting a countdown.
  • The WSPR panel has room to breathe. The stations-per-cycle strip is gone — the list already tells you the same thing — and the transmit-tone line explains itself in two lines rather than shorthand.
  • Spur removal stays on the panadapter. It works by shifting your dial 25 Hz and putting it back, and if you changed page or band mid-measurement it could put the old frequency back. It now runs only where it is useful, and never writes a frequency it has not re-checked.
  • The recovery flasher no longer erases before it checks. If you ever need flash-recovery, it now confirms every file is present before touching the chip. It previously erased first and could then fail, taking your settings and LoTW certificate with it.

!!! info "Over the air, from v1.15.0"

If you are on **v1.15.0**, this updates normally over WiFi. If you are still
on **v1.14.x or earlier**, you need the one-time USB-C flasher first — see
the v1.15.0 notes below. Pressing update on an older build will fail
harmlessly; on v1.14.0–v1.14.3 the message will not be helpful, because
those builds predate the size check.

v1.15.0 — 2026-09-18

!!! warning "This release needs a USB-C cable, once"

**v1.15.0 rewrites the partition table**, and an over-the-air update cannot
do that — it can only ever write the app, never the map of the flash. That
limit is deliberate: it is what stops a failed download taking the layout
with it.

So v1.15.0 arrives as a **flasher download**, over the same USB-C data cable
and the same script you used to install the firmware the first time. It is
the only release that needs it, and everything after it is over the air again
— with more than twice the room.

**There is no over-the-air image attached to this release, on purpose.** If
you tap the update notice it will say the download could not be reached. That
is the release refusing to be installed the wrong way, not a fault.

**Your settings, memory channels, QSO log and LoTW certificate are kept.**
Press **Enter** at the flash-type prompt — never **E**, which erases the whole
chip including your LoTW private key. **New users are unaffected**: a first
install already uses the flasher.

The band-plan slider is a window you drag, the settings backup was missing thirty-one settings, and WSPR will not beacon in split.

  • What the cable buys. The firmware had 47 KB left in its 4 MB slot — about one feature from refusing to build. Dropping a third, never-used copy of the firmware leaves two slots of 6.81 MB with 2.87 MB free. Over-the-air updates work exactly as before afterwards, alternating between the two.
  • The band-plan slider moves the window, not a dial. Grab the framed block and the whole picture travels with it — block, frequency marker and filter passband together — and it stays where you let go, with the radio following. It used to write a frequency and let the display decide where to land, so the box sprang back the moment you lifted your finger. The grab area is about 8 mm tall now rather than 4, because the strip alone was never a finger, and the passband fades back twice as fast on release.
  • Your Config download was missing 31 settings, including the power calibration (found from a question by Bruce N9JCV). That calibration is an hour at a dummy load per band and was the one thing in the file nobody could recreate from memory — it had never been included. Also added: the per-band power target, the WSPR schedule and band hopping, Field Day class and section, the activation reference, the FT8 transmit tone and twenty more. Two of them were worse than missing — the file would accept the transmit tone and its hold but never wrote them, so saving and restoring quietly reverted both.
  • Three settings reached the web page that had been Tab5-only: waterfall speed, WSPR band hopping, and whether your QMX has GPS. The last is not cosmetic — claiming it stops the Tab5 keeping the radio's clock.
  • WSPR will not beacon while the radio is in split (John W5JSS). In split the radio transmits on VFO B while still reporting VFO A, so every spot you publish names a frequency your signal was never on. The Tab5 asks the radio before each transmission and holds the burst, saying so on screen. It will not clear the split for you — that is your setting, and on the QMX it cannot be cleared over the cable anyway.
  • The WSPR transmit block was unreadable (John W5JSS): red text on an orange background, a contrast ratio of 1.15 to 1. Black on orange now. The same block sometimes kept the orange of a finished transmission while merely counting down.
  • The on-screen keyboard came back on a second tap (Samuel W7STF). Tapping a field that was already selected did nothing — nine fields across seven windows.
  • A missing SD card says so: the indicator is crossed out in grey, and tapping it explains what a card is for. A tap anywhere on the bottom bar used to open the updater.
  • The WSPR transmit schedule is two plain counts — transmit cycles and receive cycles in a repeating group — with the result written out in words as you change it. "1 in 5" meant different things to different people.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.14.4 — 2026-09-18

The reboots are fixed, countries are spelled out, and 79 callsign prefixes named the wrong country.

  • The reboots. Fifteen bench runs before the fix lasted a median of 15 minutes; with it the same bench ran 14.7 hours with none. Three rarely-read arrays sat in the small internal RAM that USB, WiFi and the SD card all need — moving them freed 17 KB. One exhaustion, arriving wherever the next allocation happened to be.
  • Opening the settings drawer cut your transmit power to WSPR's declared level and left it there.
  • Countries spelled out on the FT8 and WSPR lists, 79 prefixes corrected (Taiwan as China, Ukraine as Russia, sixteen UK prefixes as England), and stations with no grid now show an approximate distance.
  • WSPR bursts per transmission (John W5JSS), Antenna Tune shows SWR, watts and seconds left (Randy N4OPI), Calibrate Power stops at your own Max PA voltage (Bruce N9JCV), and a Flush button in the SelfSpotter header (Uwe DL8UG).

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.14.3 — 2026-09-17

Fixed a v1.14.2 crash: picking a new TX tone from the web UI while a QSO or CQ run was armed could reboot the Tab5.

  • Reproduced 100% on two benches (Randy N4OPI) - it never happened while actually transmitting, only while armed and waiting. Same underlying bug as the v1.14.0 crash - a whole settings structure copied onto a task's stack just to read one value - reached this time from the web server's own task instead of the display or CAT tasks. Fixed the same way: read one setting at a time. Reproduced and confirmed fixed on the bench before release.
  • The TX Hold checkbox not applying, reported in the same message, was very likely the same crash: tone and hold travel in one web request, and the device rebooted while handling the tone half, before hold was ever reached. Confirmed applying and reading back correctly now.
  • Output power stuck at WSPR's level after a reboot. Max. PA voltage lives in the radio and a Tab5 restart does not reset it - so if WSPR had turned it down for its declared power (as low as 2.3 V, about 200 mW) and the Tab5 was then restarted straight into FT8, everything went out at that level while the Output power slider showed the figure it was meant to be at. Handing the power back only ever happened when you left the WSPR page live, and a reboot has no such moment. The radio is now told the correct level again whenever the CAT link comes up.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.14.2 — 2026-09-17

General sluggishness since v1.13.0, root-caused — plus a web UI hang, an output-power surprise after calibration, and a SelfSpotter map bug.

  • Sluggishness some users saw starting with v1.13.0 (Randy N4OPI), including with the SelfSpotter map screen closed, root-caused: SelfSpotter's PSK Reporter feed connects over its own background task from boot regardless of whether the map is ever opened, and that task was running at a higher scheduling priority than the display, with no core assigned to it — so it could hold the display up on every incoming report. It now runs at a lower priority, pinned to the second core. Not yet confirmed fixed on Randy's own hardware.
  • The web UI's "find open slot" tool could hang on "Applying..." and lose contact with the QMX, needing a power cycle, only mid-QSO or CQ run (Randy N4OPI): a frequency-mode command could collide with an in-progress FT8/WSPR transmit burst on the radio's own control link. It now waits its turn. The page's warning text was also backwards (said it would be refused while transmitting; it actually applies automatically once the burst ends) and Apply now gives up cleanly after 8 seconds if this ever recurs.
  • Output power reading near-zero right after Calibrate Power finishes (Gyula HA3HZ) — a slider defaulted to its lowest setting and wrote that to the radio unconditionally. It now reads the radio's actual level when nothing has been chosen yet.
  • SelfSpotter: countries like Italy, Denmark and Greece drew as boxes on the map, from a coastline-simplification bug — fixed. Zoom raised 10x → 50x. The settings drawer's own content was taller than the panel and silently hid the Flush button — fixed. A screenshot of the map now carries your callsign, dial frequency and UTC time in its own header line (Gyula HA3HZ), and every screenshot download gets a timestamped filename.
  • Colour cleanup: the map, the Live Spots lane and the network drawer's spot checkboxes now share one colour scheme instead of three that had drifted apart.
  • Waterfall scroll speed is now a real setting (1x–4x) instead of a fixed rate.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.14.1 — 2026-09-16

A fix for a v1.14.0 crash on tuning or QMX power-on.

  • Fixed a crash reported by Martin Howard and Rick Trommer W5NR - thanks to both for the quick reports. spots_any_source_enabled() copied the whole settings struct onto a task stack as small as 4096 bytes — the render task, and independently the CAT poll task, either of which runs on nearly every frequency change — overflowing it on almost any tuning motion, or the frequency update an immediate QMX reconnect sends. Fixed by Uwe DL8UG: four narrow getters reading one bool each, instead of the whole struct. If you are running v1.14.0, please update.

docs.title: Previous Releases
docs.text:
v1.14.0 — 2026-09-16

Calibrate Power: WSPR Declared power now fits what the QMX actually does, as closely as its own protocol allows.

  • Calibrate Power, a new drawer feature: sweeps the QMX's Max. PA voltage through 45 points (1.0–12.0 V) on a dummy load, keying a real DiGi TX;/TA;/RX; carrier at each point — the same primitives a WSPR/FT8 burst is built from — and recording the real measured RF output from the radio's own PC; readback.
