"cw" is refused with HTTP 403 while the CW page is switched off set_ft8_mode mode: "ft8"/"ft4", optional freq_hz Switch between FT8 and FT4, optionally retuning. Omit freq_hz to keep the current frequency. This is an action rather than a setting because it also retunes the radio and clears stale decodes — read ft8_op_mode back from /api/settings to confirm set_activation ref Set the POTA/SOTA activation reference cw_adopt call Set the station the CW page is working - the callsign {CALL} sends in a macro. The web equivalent of typing it on the Tab5's station card, for when the signal is too weak to decode. An empty call clears it. Letters, digits and / only, 15 at most; anything else is refused with HTTP 400. Answers {"ok":true,"target":"..."}. The current station, the last decoded callsign and the report copied from the station are in /api/status under cw_tx (target, heard, heard_age_s, rst_rcvd) cw_send text Send CW. A macro with its fields still in it, or free text. The text is added to a queue (256 characters), so a second call while the radio keys is sent after the first. Keys the radio, and passes the band guard at that moment. Acted on only while the Tab5 is on the CW page. HTTP 400 with no text, HTTP 409 {"ok":false,"err":"CW queue full"} when the queue is full (queue from v1.26.0) cw_cancel (none) Drop the CW text that the radio has not been given yet. Answers {"ok":true,"dropped":N}. It cannot stop what the radio already holds (80 characters at most) (v1.26.0) cw_macro_edit idx (0-5), text Write one of the six macros of the active set log_qso call, optional rst_sent, rst_rcvd, name, qth, comment Log a CW or SSB contact worked by hand, as the Tab5's own Log window does. name, qth and comment are what the other operator told you (ADIF NAME, QTH, COMMENT; 24, 24 and 60 bytes, longer text is cut). Nothing else is accepted: the frequency, mode, band, date, time, your callsign, your grid and the running activation are read from the device, so a page holding a stale frequency cannot write a record on the wrong band. An empty report logs no report rather than a wrong one. Refused with HTTP 400 and a reason when the callsign is empty or there is no CAT. Answers {"ok":true,"call":"...","act_qsos":N,"act_need":N,"total":N}, so the count needs no second request cq_start (none) Start a CQ run, as the Tab5's own Call CQ button does. Keys the radio. Only acted on while the Tab5 is in FT8/FT4 mode; otherwise discarded, not queued reply call Work a decoded station — the same intelligent Transmit a Tab5 row-tap runs. Keys the radio. Outcome in /api/status ft8.web_r qso_override what: "resend"/"rr73"/"73"/"cancel"/"pause"/"skip" Mid-QSO override, as the Tab5's own buttons do. pause skips one transmission; skip gives up on this caller and keeps answering others. Keys the radio except for cancel, pause and skip clear_swr (none) Clear a latched SWR-protection trip, same as tapping the Tab5's own fault prompt. TX stays refused until this is called tune_start / tune_stop (none) Antenna Tune (QMX 1.04+ only). Keys the radio continuously; 60 s safety stop on the device. While running, /api/status carries a tune object with watts, swr and secs (seconds left before the safety stop); the object is absent when no tune is running pause / resume (none) Release the radio so its own menus can be used, and take it back. While paused the CAT poll, the dead-stream watchdog and the stuck-decode watchdog all stand down greylist_clear (none) Un-skip every grey-listed station ota_install url Download and install firmware. Refused while transmitting or mid-QSO, with the reason in the reply body. Does not restart on its own ota_reboot (none) Restart into firmware already installed usb_shutdown (none) Orderly USB teardown before a reflash: radio to RX, CAT and audio closed, VBUS dropped usb_replug (none) Power-cycle the USB port to recover a wedged device power_off (none) Power the Tab5 down reset_settings (none) Clear stored settings back to defaults reset_network (none) Clear the stored WiFi/network state

Radio menus (the QMX's own terminal, on its second serial port): term_view, qmx_ports and qmx_term_probe are /api/cmd actions. open, close, key and text are actions of POST /api/term, not of /api/cmd. See Radio menus and GET /api/term.

Developer actions. No button on the web page sends these (the page sends resmon on Ctrl+Alt+R), and they are easy to regret:

Action Effect cat_raw Send one raw CAT string to the radio drawer Open the settings drawer, optionally at scroll_y, so a section below the fold can be screenshotted resmon Toggle the resource-monitor overlay time_redetect Re-arm the once-per-boot QMX GPS detection without rebooting help Open the on-device manual at a topic panic_test Crash the device deliberately, to prove the crash recorder works. ⚠ Radio off only — a panic reboot is a warm reset, which leaves the QMX needing a power cycle

⚠ Check the response BODY as well as the status code. The reply is {"ok":true} on success. An unrecognised action is refused with HTTP 400 and the text unknown action. A refused action (for example ota_install while transmitting) can still answer HTTP 200 with {"ok":false,"error":"..."}, so a caller that only tests the status code cannot tell success from a refusal. A few CW and JS8 actions name the reason err instead of error.

The request body can be 1024 bytes at most (v1.26.0; it was cut at 255 before, without an error). A longer body is refused with HTTP 413. An empty body is HTTP 400 no body, and invalid JSON is HTTP 400 bad json.

display.peak_hold_s is the spectrum peak-hold window in seconds, 0 = off, maximum 60. The Tab5 drawer offers 1, 2, 3 and 5; the API accepts any value in range. It is also in /api/status as peak_hold_s, so a browser can follow a change made on the Tab5 without re-reading the settings.

Spectrum smoothing has two names for one stored value. display.smooth_pct is the operator-facing one: 0 is off, higher is smoother, and it is what the settings form shows. display.ema_pct is the raw EMA coefficient × 100, where 100 means no smoothing — the inverse. Both are reported by GET /api/settings and both are accepted by the POST; if a payload carries both, smooth_pct wins. ema_pct is kept because config files and scripts written before 2026-10-24 use it, and /api/status reports it under wf.ema_pct for a browser drawing its own trace.

A missing required parameter is refused with HTTP 400. set_freq, set_band, set_bw, set_zoom, set_rit and view_center answer <key> required (number) when the key is absent or is sent as a string. Until 2026-10-23 they answered {"ok":true} and did nothing, so {"action":"set_freq","freq":10000000} looked like a successful tune. set_screen likewise refuses a name it does not know instead of falling back to the panadapter.

Effects are applied asynchronously — mode and filter writes are queued onto the CAT poll task, and cq_start, reply, qso_override and set_ft8_mode onto the display task — so read /api/status or /api/settings to see the result rather than assuming it from the response.

docs.title: GET /api/tone
docs.text:
The TX audio tone and the live occupancy of the 200-2800 Hz window.

{ "hz": 1650, "hold": false, "min": 200, "max": 2800, "step": 50,
  "stations": 14, "busy": "0000000000111110...", "partner_hz": 1750, "busy_tx": false }

busy is one character per 50 Hz slot (1 = a station or its guard band), sent as a string because 52 bits do not survive JavaScript's number type. busy_e and busy_o carry the EVEN and ODD windows separately — two stations only collide in the same window, and only the operator knows which one they are about to transmit into; busy remains the our-window/union view the automatic verdict uses. stations is how many decoded stations fed the mask - zero means the band picture is unknown, not empty, and a caller must say so rather than showing the all-clear.

docs.title: POST /api/tone
docs.text:
{"hz":1650} and/or {"hold":true}. Out-of-range frequencies are clamped.

A tone change while a QSO is running is applied to the running exchange first (your partner tracks your slot, not your tone). Mid-burst it is refused with 409 and the body carries the device's own reason - the preference is not stored either, so the two can never end up half-committed.

docs.title: GET /api/memory
docs.text: All 32 memory channels: {"slots":[{"idx":0,"occupied":true,"freq_hz":14074000,"mode":"DIGI","label":"FT8"}, ...]}. Empty slots carry only idx and occupied:false.

docs.title: POST /api/memory
docs.text:
Write one channel - {"idx":3,"freq_hz":14074000,"mode":"DIGI","label":"FT8"} - or clear one with {"idx":3,"clear":true}. Fields you omit keep their stored value, so renaming a channel needs only idx and label.

A frequency outside a recognised amateur band returns 400 - the same refusal the Tab5 makes, so the browser cannot be a way around it.

There is no recall endpoint: recalling a channel is set_freq plus set_mode, which /api/cmd already does.

docs.title: GET /api/settings
docs.text:
The settings a browser can usefully edit: callsign, grid, the CQ presets, the FT8 filters, the everyday toggles, QMX volume, band-plan region and the WiFi SSID. The spot sources (spots_en overall, then rbn_en and cluster_en), propagation feedback (psk_rx_en) and the Bluetooth mouse (bt_mouse_en) are here too — bt_mouse_en is stored immediately but only takes effect after a restart. swr_limit_x10 is the SWR limit × 10, so 30 is 3.0:1. It is writable: 0 switches SWR protection off, and any other value is held between 20 and 40.

The WiFi password is never returned - only wifi_pass_set says whether one is stored.

docs.title: POST /api/settings
docs.text:
Applies a partial update: only the keys present are touched, everything else is left alone. So a single toggle is a one-key body, and a stale browser form can never reset fields it did not show.

{ "my_grid": "JO65ab", "rbn_en": true, "cq": { "max_calls": 10 } }

wifi_ssid and wifi_pass take effect only when both are supplied - an empty password means "keep the stored one", never "erase it". qmx_vol_db is in dB (0-50) and is sent to the radio as well as stored.

Everything the settings drawer can change is reachable here. Besides the keys above that includes flat_mode, distance_in_miles, greylist_en, ft8_early_decode, field_day_en (with fd_class / fd_section), spots_en, sota_en, rbn_en, pskreporter_en, resmon_en, tx_tone_hold, tx_tone_hz, cw_pitch_hz and cw_cal_hz — all readable back from GET.

sim_mode_en is the one to know about if you are automating tests. With it on, the firmware runs complete FT8 exchanges against phantom stations and ft8_tx.c hard-refuses to key the radio, so a QSO can be driven end to end with no antenna and no QMX attached. ⚠ Simulated contacts land in the real ADIF log, so turn it off afterwards and delete them — they have FREQ=0, and the ADIF viewer's "Del N test" button finds exactly those.

Read-only reporters. ft8_op_mode ("ft8" / "ft4") and ft8_freq_hz are returned but not writable here — change them with the set_ft8_mode action, which also retunes the radio and clears stale decodes, then read these back to confirm.

docs.title: GET /api/decodes
docs.text:
The FT8/FT4 decode list as the Tab5 shows it - same ordering (the station being worked, then messages addressed to you, then CQ calls, then strongest signal) and the same Filter-window hides applied. Read-only.

{
  "mode": "FT8",
  "miles": false,
  "working": "DK7CVD",
  "rows": [
    { "call": "DK7CVD", "text": "OZ1LAV DK7CVD -07", "grid": "JO31",
      "snr": -7, "hz": 1503, "dt": 210, "age": 6, "heard": 3,
      "km": 612, "brg": 173,
      "sl": "E", "me": true, "cq": false, "pin": true }
  ]
}

dt is milliseconds, hz the station's audio tone, age seconds since it was last decoded, sl the transmit window it was heard in. me marks a message containing your callsign, pin the station you are working.

km and brg (v1.8.3) are distance and bearing from your grid to theirs, worked out on the device with the same maths the Tab5's own list uses. Both are omitted entirely when either grid is missing — there is no null and no zero, so a client should render an absent field as "unknown" rather than as a distance. km is in miles when the top-level miles flag is true, which mirrors the Distance in miles setting.

docs.title: GET /api/help
docs.text:
The guidance rows, ranked by the device from its own live state. flagged marks a row the firmware can see is happening right now.

{
  "context": { "page": "guide/panadapter.md", "anchor": "Layout", "label": "Panadapter" },
  "rows": [
    { "symptom": "My radio is not showing up", "flagged": true,
      "page": "reference/troubleshooting.md", "anchor": "won't reconnect",
      "label": "Radio not connecting" }
  ]
}

context is the chapter the Tab5's own User Manual button would open right now. anchor is a case-insensitive heading substring, not a URL fragment.

docs.title: GET /api/manual?page=guide/ft8-tx.md
docs.text: One page of the built-in manual, as the raw markdown that built the documentation site. page=toc.json returns the contents list. Served from the firmware, so it needs no internet and always matches the running version. 404 if the page is not in this firmware's manual.

docs.title: CAT Endpoints
docs.text: Send CAT-level changes through POST /api/cmd (set_freq, set_mode, set_bw, set_band), which routes them through the CAT poll task - the only writer to the radio's serial port. For one raw CAT string there is the developer action cat_raw with a cmd field; its reply appears in the diagnostic log, and a command that would transmit passes the band guard first.

docs.title: FT8 Endpoints
docs.text: The decode list is GET /api/decodes (above). Transmit from the browser is limited to POST /api/cmd {"action":"cq_start"}; there is no endpoint that sends an arbitrary FT8 message, deliberately - replies are chosen from the decode list in front of you, at the Tab5.

docs.title: GET /api/adif
docs.text:
Download ADIF log.

Response: ADIF file (text/plain)

?activation=<REF> limits the download to contacts made during an activation of that reference (matched on MY_SIG_INFO), so a park's log can be uploaded on its own rather than the whole file. An unknown reference returns a valid ADIF file with no records, not an error.

?date=today or ?date=YYYYMMDD limits it to one UTC day, and names the download qso-YYYY-MM-DD.adi so a daily file is self-identifying once it is saved. A day with no contacts returns a valid empty ADIF, not an error.

docs.title: POST /api/adif/import
docs.text:
Restore records from a raw ADIF file — the browser's own "ADIF download", or any other logger's export. Body is the ADIF text itself (Content-Type: text/plain).

?mark_uploaded=0 imports the contacts as not yet uploaded, so the next QRZ/ eQSL/LoTW upload pass sends them. Default (1, or the parameter omitted) marks them as already uploaded instead — advancing all three upload cursors to the new record count — since the ordinary reason to restore a log is that these contacts were already sent before whatever wiped the device.

A pretty-printed, multi-line record (as some loggers export) is normalised to this device's own one-line-per-record form before being written. A record whose CALL+QSO_DATE+TIME_ON already matches one in the log is skipped, so re-importing the same file twice — or a file that overlaps an earlier partial restore — adds nothing extra.

Response:

{ "ok": true, "added": 12, "total": 47 }

added: 0 with ok: true means every record in the file was already logged. ok: false means the log could not be written at all (storage full).

docs.title: POST /api/adif/edit
docs.text:
Correct one field of one record: ?idx=<n>&call=<CALL>&field=<F>&value=<V>.

idx is the record's position in the file and call must match the callsign already stored there — both, or the device answers 409 and changes nothing, so a browser showing a stale list cannot edit the wrong QSO.

Any ADIF field can be edited. The field name can hold letters, digits and underscore only. RST_SENT, RST_RCVD, GRIDSQUARE, QSO_DATE and TIME_ON are format-checked, and a value that does not fit is refused with 400. An empty value removes the field, which for a report is the honest record of one that was never exchanged. SIG_INFO is the reference the other station was activating (US-1241, G/LD-049, DLFF-0123); the device derives SIG from its shape and writes it alongside, and clears it again when the reference is cleared. Callsign, band, mode, date and time are what QRZ, eQSL and LoTW match a contact on, so a change to one of them here does not change the copy a logbook already holds.

Response: {"ok":true}, or {"ok":false,"error":"…"}

docs.title: POST /api/adif/clear
docs.text:
Clear all QSOs from ADIF log.

Response:

{"ok": true}

docs.title: GET /api/config
docs.text:
Download current configuration (all settings + memory channels).

Response: INI text file

docs.title: POST /api/config
docs.text:
Upload a configuration file to restore settings.

Request: the config file as the raw request body (not multipart)

Response:

{"applied": 57}

applied is the number of settings the file changed.

docs.title: GET /api/log
docs.text:
Download diagnostic log.

Response: Text file (qmx-log.txt)

docs.title: GET /api/log/saved
docs.text:
The flash-persisted copy of the diagnostic log from before the last reboot or power-off - the one that survives a crash in the field.

Response: Text file

docs.title: GET /api/signal
docs.text:
The signal level alone, for a faster S-meter than the 1 Hz /api/status poll can give. Same DSP call and parameters as /api/status and the Tab5's own S-meter - only the cadence differs.

{ "dbm": -83.5 }

docs.title: GET /api/sched
docs.text:
The contest calendar and announced ?OTA activations on one timeline, soonest first — the same list, sort and source names the Tab5's Scheduled events pane draws, because both read sched_events_get().

{ "age_s": 240, "busy": false, "version": 3, "wifi": true, "now": 1785340050,
  "events": [
    { "what": "CQ WW DX SSB", "src": "WA7BNM Contest Calendar",
      "srcs": "WA7BNM", "start": 1785344400, "end": 1785517200,
      "contest": true },
    { "what": "OZ1LAV", "ref": "DL-0123", "src": "POTA", "srcs": "POTA",
      "start": 1785341000, "end": 0, "contest": false }
  ] }

srcs is the shortened form for a column ("WA7BNM Contest Calendar" → "WA7BNM"); src is the full name the record carries. ref is omitted for a contest. start or end of 0 means the feed gave no usable time.

Events already finished are dropped; one with no usable end time is kept. No filtering here — contest is the flag, and the All / Contests / ?OTA choice belongs to whichever surface is drawing.

Requesting this asks for a refresh, but the 15-minute floor is enforced on the device, so polling cannot reach the upstream feed faster than that. Add ?force=1 for the pane's own Refresh button. The fetch runs on the spots task, so the call returns at once with whatever is already held.

now is the device's clock, and a countdown should be computed against it: a browser clock minutes out would show rows as running that the Tab5 still shows as upcoming.

The upstream feed being down is an ordinary state, not an error. There is no error field: busy, age_s (-1 = never fetched) and version (0 = never fetched) are what tell "slow" apart from "nothing scheduled".

docs.title: GET /api/psk_rx
docs.text:
Propagation feedback — which receivers have copied your call, from PSK Reporter.

{ "enabled": true, "age_s": 96, "receivers": 14, "max_km": 7412,
  "reports": [
    { "call": "W1ABC", "grid": "FN42", "dxcc": "United States", "mode": "FT8",
      "f": 14074812, "t": 1785340050, "snr": -14, "km": 6031, "brg": 291 }
  ] }

Requesting this asks for a refresh, but the collector's own five-minute floor is enforced on the device, so polling faster than that returns the same data with a larger age_s rather than fetching again. age_s is -1 before the first successful query.

snr is omitted when the receiver gave none — 0 dB is a real report, so it cannot double as "unknown". km and brg are omitted together when the receiver's grid is unknown.

Off by default. The endpoint always answers: with the feature disabled nothing is fetched, so enabled is false and reports holds whatever the last query returned before it was switched off — read age_s rather than assuming the list is current. It is also empty while offline or before a callsign is set.

docs.title:
POST /api/adif/delete?idx=&call=

Delete one QSO. Both the index and the callsign must match the record, or the request is refused with 409 - so a stale browser view can never delete the wrong contact.

GET /api/upload_status

Progress of a running QRZ/eQSL/LoTW upload (busy, kind, uploaded, failed, error).

POST /api/qrz_key

Set QRZ API key (stored server-side).

Request: the key itself as the raw request body - plain text, not JSON, 47 characters at most.

POST /api/qrz_upload

Upload ADIF to QRZ Logbook.

Response: HTTP 202 with {"status":"uploading"}. The upload runs in the background; read the result from GET /api/upload_status, which reports busy, kind, uploaded, failed, error and sometimes a note. While another upload is running the answer is HTTP 423 upload in progress.

POST /api/eqsl_upload

Upload ADIF to eQSL.

Response: HTTP 202 with {"status":"uploading"}. The upload runs in the background; read the result from GET /api/upload_status, which reports busy, kind, uploaded, failed, error and sometimes a note. While another upload is running the answer is HTTP 423 upload in progress.

POST /api/lotw_cert

Store the LoTW callsign certificate and key (extracted from the TQSL .p12 in the browser during LoTW setup).

POST /api/lotw_upload

Sign all pending QSOs with the stored certificate and upload them to lotw.arrl.org.

Response: HTTP 202 with {"status":"uploading"}. The upload runs in the background; read the result from GET /api/upload_status, which reports busy, kind, uploaded, failed, error and sometimes a note. While another upload is running the answer is HTTP 423 upload in progress.

GET /api/lotw_tq8

Download the whole log as a signed .tq8 file, for manual upload to LoTW or offline verification.

Response: .tq8 file (gzipped, signed)
WebSocket (Streaming)
docs.text:
Single-client endpoint for live spectrum:

ws://<tab5-ip>:80/ws

There are three kinds of binary frame. The first byte says which.

First byte Frame 0x01 Spectrum 0x02 Takeover notice: another client has taken the stream, and this one must stop reconnecting 0x03 Receiver audio

Spectrum frame, 1063 bytes:

Bytes Meaning 0 0x01 1 Zoom decimation factor (1 = base 1024-bin spectrum, >1 = zoom-FFT with that decimation) 2–5 Dial frequency, Hz, for this capture 6–9 Left edge of the view, Hz 10–13 Span, Hz 14–17, 18–21 Lowest and highest frequency the radio can hear, Hz 22–23 IF offset, Hz, signed 24–1047 1024 unsigned bytes, one per bin, quantised −130 dBm (0) to −30 dBm (255) 1048–1062 Trailer. Its first two bytes are the S-meter: signal in dBm × 10, signed 16-bit, little-endian, 0x8000 = no reading. The rest is view state for the page

Bins are pre-shifted server-side, so byte 24 is the leftmost screen pixel and a client does not have to know where the VFO sits in the FFT. Push rate is about 10 fps.

Audio frame (sent only while a client has asked to listen): byte 0 is 0x03, bytes 2–3 a sequence number, bytes 4–5 the sample rate (12000), and from byte 6 the samples, µ-law, mono.

!!! warning "One client at a time" A second connection takes the stream over from the first, which receives one frame of type 0x02. Opening the web UI in two tabs is enough to do it. A connect can also be refused when the Tab5 is short of memory; try again after 2 seconds.

docs.title:
GET /rnnoise.wasm

The speech model for the browser's noise reduction, as WebAssembly. The page fetches it once, the first time the speech model is switched on.

Noise reduction and the auto-notch have no setting on the Tab5 and no API. They run in the browser and their settings are stored in the browser. See Web DSP.

GET /ss.bmp

Returns what is on the Tab5's screen right now, as a BMP.

Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://192.168.1.213/ss.bmp" -OutFile screenshot.bmp

!!! note "It freezes animations while it reads" The screen is captured from the live framebuffer, so a waterfall or a blinking indicator stops for the duration of the read.
Error Responses
docs.text:
There is no single error format. An error is one of two things:

  • a plain-text body with an HTTP error status, for example 400 with unknown action;
  • a JSON body {"ok":false,"error":"..."}, sometimes with HTTP 200. A few CW and JS8 actions use the key err.

Common HTTP status codes:

  • 200 — Success, or a refusal that says so in the body
  • 202 — An upload was started
  • 400 — Bad request (unknown action, missing or invalid argument)
  • 403 — The feature is switched off
  • 409 — The request does not match the device's state (wrong record, queue full)
  • 413 — The request body is too long
  • 423 — An upload is already running
  • 500 — Server error

docs.title: Example: Tune to 7.074 MHz in Python
docs.text:
import requests

ip = "192.168.1.50"
api = f"http://{ip}/api"

# Set frequency
requests.post(f"{api}/cmd", json={"action": "set_freq", "hz": 7074000})

# Set mode
requests.post(f"{api}/cmd", json={"action": "set_mode", "mode": "USB"})

# Check status
status = requests.get(f"{api}/status").json()
print(f"Now on {status['freq_hz']} Hz, {status['mode']} mode")

Next: See Troubleshooting for API debugging.
